text:
Because the π⁺ is at rest, its total energy is just its rest-mass energy  

Eπ = mπc² = 139.6 MeV.

When it decays to a massive muon and an (essentially) mass-zero neutrino,

π⁺ → μ⁺ + νμ ,

energy–momentum conservation fixes the final energies uniquely (two–body decay).

Let p be the magnitude of the common momentum of the two decay products.  
Using natural units (c = 1), we have

1) Energy conservation: mπ = Eμ + Eν  
2) Momentum conservation: pμ = pν = p

For the neutrino (m ≈ 0): Eν = p.  
For the muon: Eμ² = p² + mμ².

Solve for p:

p = (mπ² − mμ²) / (2mπ).

Insert the given masses (MeV/c²):

mπ = 139.6, mμ = 105.7  
mπ² = 139.6² = 1.9488×10⁴  
mμ² = 105.7² = 1.1172×10⁴

p = (1.9488×10⁴ − 1.1172×10⁴) / (2 × 139.6)  
  = 8.3156×10³ / 279.2  
  ≃ 29.8 MeV.

Hence

Eν = p ≃ 29.8 MeV,

Eμ = √(p² + mμ²)  
    = √(29.8² + 105.7²) ≃ 109.8 MeV.

Muon kinetic energy:  
Tμ = Eμ − mμ = 109.8 − 105.7 ≃ 4.1 MeV.

So

K.E.(μ⁺) ≃ 4.1 MeV, K.E.(νμ) ≃ 29.8 MeV.

These match option (A).

Answer: A
